symptoms: The class is present and the method is not, which no missing-jar explanation covers
The failure appears after a runtime upgrade with no change to the job's own code
The named method belongs to an interface the job never calls directly
likely_causes: Two versions of the same artifact are on the classpath, and the one that won does not implement a method added later
A connector compiled against an older interface runs against a newer runtime
User jars take precedence over the runtime's own, so an older implementation shadows the newer one
diagnostic_steps: List every jar on the classpath and look for two that carry the same package: this error is the signature of a duplicate, not of an absence
Read whether user jars take precedence: spark.driver.userClassPathFirst and spark.executor.userClassPathFirst default to false and are documented as experimental
Compare the interface version the connector was compiled against with the one the runtime provides
fixes: Remove the older copy of the artifact from the classpath, so only one implementation remains
Rebuild the connector against the interface the current runtime provides
Reconsider giving user jars precedence: the Spark documentation marks that behaviour as experimental, and it is what lets an older implementation win
unsafe_fixes: Turning user class path precedence on to force the older artifact to win: it makes this failure disappear by moving the conflict to whatever the runtime expected from the newer interface
verification: Re-run the job and exercise the code path that calls the method, and confirm only one copy of the artifact is on the classpath
rollback: Restore the previous classpath. It changes no data, but a third-party artifact swapped for another release line can change the value of what it produces, and that needs comparing
